common_name: Glacier Falls Heucherella (Trailing Blue-Green Foamy Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Glacier Falls is part of Terra Nova's trailing Falls series, bred to spill rather than mound.

directions: Glacier Falls is a trailing foamy bells from Terra Nova Nurseries' Falls series, with soft, fuzzy, frosted blue-green leaves marked by darker veining that spill 18 inches or more over a container edge or rock wall. Small white flower spikes appear in early summer above the foliage mat, but the trailing, groundcover-forming leaves are the main draw. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade, where its vigorous spreading habit makes it useful as both a hanging-basket spiller and a dense groundcover. Shear back leggy runners after flowering to keep the mat tight and encourage fresh foliage color.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil; Twilight tolerates more sun than most heucherella, from full shade to nearly full sun given adequate moisture.

directions: Twilight is a Terra Nova Nurseries selection grown for velvety, smoky charcoal-gray leaves overlaid with burgundy and silver shading, a moodier palette than the typical gold- or copper-toned heucherella. It forms a low, symmetrical, well-branched mound and sends up slender spikes of small white flowers from late spring into summer. Unusually for the genus it was bred for rust resistance and tolerates everything from full shade to considerable sun, though the darkest foliage color develops with some protection from the hottest afternoon rays. Keep soil consistently moist and divide congested clumps every few years in spring.

common_name: Fire Frost Heucherella (Villosa-Type Foamy Bells with Red Center)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; its Heuchera villosa parentage gives Fire Frost above-average heat and humidity tolerance for a heucherella.

directions: Fire Frost is a Terra Nova Nurseries heucherella bred using Heuchera villosa, which gives it a larger, more upright habit and much better tolerance of summer heat and humidity than typical foamy bells. Leaves open yellow-green to lime with a bold red center and a frosty overlay of white veiling, holding color well into fall. Airy stalks of tiny white flowers rise well above the foliage from midsummer into early fall. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; it accepts more sun and heat than most heucherella but still benefits from afternoon shade in hot climates and consistent moisture.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Honey Rose, bred by Janet Egger at Terra Nova Nurseries, holds its deeply cut leaf pattern year-round in mild climates.

directions: Honey Rose is a compact, neat Terra Nova Nurseries heucherella whose deeply lobed, dark-veined leaves open warm coral-rose in spring and mature to a honeyed, sable-brown by summer. Masses of small white flowers rise on wiry stalks just above the foliage from early to midsummer. Its tidy, slow-spreading clump stays in bounds, making it well suited to edging, containers, and small-space mixed beds rather than groundcover use. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and divide every few years in spring once the center of the clump becomes congested.

common_name: Jade Peacock Foamflower (Seasonally Color-Changing Compact Tiarella)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Jade Peacock forms a dense, non-spreading clump rather than running by stolons like many groundcover foamflowers.

directions: Jade Peacock is a Proven Winners foamflower selected for evergreen foliage that shifts dramatically through the seasons: new spring leaves open bright yellow-green with a deep red center, mature to jade green with a purple center through summer, and turn mahogany-purple with a near-black center for winter. Its tight, clumping habit holds its shape in the garden rather than wandering, distinguishing it from runner-type tiarella groundcovers. Lightly fragrant, star-shaped white flowers open from pink buds on short spikes above the foliage from early to midspring. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in dappled to full shade, and mulch to keep roots cool and moist through summer.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Stargazer Mercury is a compact, clump-forming selection in Proven Winners' Stargazer foamflower series.

directions: Stargazer Mercury is a compact foamflower with deeply cut, star-shaped green leaves marked by dark striping along the midribs of each finger-like lobe, forming a tidy mound that stays in place rather than spreading by runners. In mid-spring, wiry, mostly leafless stems rise above the foliage carrying small pink flowers in bottlebrush-like racemes. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, siting it where its finely textured, patterned foliage can be appreciated at the front of a woodland border or in a shaded container. Mulch to conserve moisture, since shallow-rooted tiarella decline quickly in dry soil.

common_name: Nova Cobalt Pulmonaria (Deep Blue Spring-Flowering Lungwort)

planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Nova Cobalt is a Terra Nova Nurseries selection valued for unusually deep, saturated blue flower color.

directions: Nova Cobalt is a Terra Nova Nurseries lungwort grown for clusters of red buds that open into bell-shaped flowers of an intensely deep, true blue, held above white-spotted, elliptic green leaves. The clumping, non-invasive habit makes it a reliable, long-lived groundcover under deciduous shrubs and trees where little else blooms so early. Its spring display is a strong early-season draw for hummingbirds just returning north. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and divide congested clumps right after flowering to maintain vigor and increase the planting.

common_name: Silver Scimitar Pulmonaria (Arching Strap-Leaf Sun-Tolerant Lungwort)

planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, well-drained soil; Silver Scimitar, bred by Terra Nova Nurseries, tolerates more sun than most lungworts but still needs protection from hot afternoon exposure.

directions: Silver Scimitar is a Terra Nova Nurseries lungwort with large, arching, wavy-edged strap-shaped leaves in solid silvery green rather than the spotted pattern typical of most pulmonaria. In early spring it produces a tight mound of bicolor pink-and-purple, bell-shaped flowers that draw early hummingbirds just as the foliage is emerging. It was bred for improved powdery mildew tolerance and handles more sun than typical lungworts, though afternoon shade still helps prevent leaf scorch in hot climates. Grow in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil, and divide crowded clumps after flowering to keep the planting vigorous.
